text: Three buttons sound alike but do very different things. Picking the wrong one leaves money taken with nothing given back.
Here are the payments on this bill.
Refund gives money back. Void fixes a mistake. And refund before you void a bill.
Click Refund next to the card payment.
Refund sends money back to the card through Stripe.
Partial is fine. A reason is optional here, but it's a good habit.
We won't refund now. Click Cancel.
Now click Void next to the cash payment.
Void is for a payment recorded by mistake, like cash typed on the wrong bill. It needs a reason.
We'll leave it for now. Click Cancel.
Now try to void the whole bill. Click Void invoice.
Scout won't void a bill that's paid by card. Refund first.
A voided bill shows its items as voided on the pet's chart. Reopen it to bill them again.

The most common mistakes are voiding a paid bill instead of refunding, and using refund to fix a payment that was recorded wrong. Remember: refund to give money back, void a payment to fix a recording mistake, and refund before you void a bill.
